correctness.rationale: For connected d-regular graphs, adjacency trace identities and the eigenvalue interval [-d,d) give tr(AL+) >= (N-3d)/(2d), with equality excluded by the second moment at N=3d. Since tr(AL+)=2 sum over edges L+uv, an edge with positive L+uv exists. The scalar Gauss [2/2] stability expansion is R(hλ)=1-12/(hλ)+O(h^-2) on nonzero modes, hence Tuv becomes negative; R(hλ) is strictly positive <=1 for all positive hλ. The torus is degree four and order mn; all nonexceptional tori have mn>=12. For C3 square C3 the exact three-eigenspace projectors lead to manifestly positive formulas. Boundaries h=0 and mn=12 checked. Exact-rational regression of 7 graphs/35 steps supports but does not prove the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The threshold N>=3d is a natural scale-free universal structural obstruction for preserving nonnegative graph diffusion with an A-stable fourth-order numerical method. It yields a sharp qualitative complete classification on all periodic square tori and a trace/Green-kernel mechanism for how spectral stability coexists with negative numerical transitions. This is more than a routine isolated example or arbitrary finite parameter computation.
